Care

Keeping it.

Natural cloth changes with wear. Most of what follows is about letting it do that in the right direction.

By cloth

GarmentClothCare
Sculpted Wool Coat Wool flannel Dry clean only · Brush after wear · Rest on a broad hanger
Tailored Flannel Trouser Wool flannel Dry clean · Press on the reverse · Hang by the hem
Poplin Atelier Shirt Cotton poplin Machine wash 30° · Iron damp · Do not tumble dry
Merino Rib Top Merino rib Hand wash cool · Dry flat · Never hang
Linen Field Jacket Linen canvas Machine wash 30° · Line dry · Press while damp
Silk Crepe Dress Silk crepe Dry clean only · Store on a padded hanger

Questions

Asked often.

Thirty days, postage paid, no reason needed. We would rather you sent it back than kept something that does not work — but the fit page exists so that happens as rarely as possible.

Because it is meant to be. It is cut 6 cm under the body measurement and stretches to meet it. Sizing up gives you a looser top, not a better-fitting one.

Not usually. Runs are cut once, in the quantity the cloth allows, and when a cloth is finished the garment is finished with it.

Yes, and it is supposed to. It is wet-finished so it softens and marks where it has been worn. If you want linen that stays flat, this is not it.

Hems and sleeve length, yes, in the Porto workshop, at cost. Anything structural is usually better cut new — write to us and we will say honestly which of the two it is.

Cloth first, then the cut.
